correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed: positive spine support is forced; every selected spine index forces its leaf; omitted spine indices with one selected path neighbor force their leaf; any optional leaf at a vertex with two selected path neighbors violates inclusion-minimality. For T subset S, the only possible new leaves occur at two-neighbor holes, creating auxiliary equality edges. Proper canonical subforts correspond exactly to unions of connected components, so minimal sets are exactly connected even-step intervals. Exact two-boundary size and summation cover n>=1 including odd/even endpoint cases. Independent brute force checked all 349524 subsets of n=1..9 under the original fort condition and full subfort minimality, not just pattern tests. Finite checks are not infinite proof.

value.rationale: In the fort-cover model of zero forcing, minimal forts are the irredundant family of combinatorial obstructions. The comb P_n corona K1 is a canonical widely used caterpillar and directly appears as an example in the original fort paper. The exact family structure, complete fort-size polynomial and quadratic count for every n are nontrivial structured facts, contrasting with exponential minimal-fort counts of ordinary paths and not implied numerically by a generic tree upper bound. All sizes and every labeled constraint are determined, enabling direct construction without enumerating 2^(2n) possible subsets.
